segmenti.tekst: نَحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ أَحْسَنَ الْقَصَصِ بِمَا أَوْحَيْنَا إِلَيْكَ هَٰذَا الْقُرْآنَ وَإِنْ كُنْتَ مِنْ قَبْلِهِ لَمِنَ الْغَافِلِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “We relate to you the best of stories in revealing to you this Qur’an, though before it you were among the unaware.” (Yusuf 12:3)

segmenti.tekst: الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ رَبِّ الْعَالَمِينَ وَالصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ عَلَى نَبِيِّنَا مُحَمَّدٍ وَعَلَى آلِهِ وَصَحْبِهِ
segmenti.prevod: Praise be to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon his family and companions.

segmenti.tekst: This morning, that is, at this last Fajr prayer of this month of Ramadan, we are completing the tafsir (exegesis) of Surah Yusuf.
That is, we have completed the tafsir of Surah Yusuf as a story, where Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, ends this story with a beautiful ending, where Yusuf and his family are finally reunited

and remain living in Egypt. After that, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, addresses our Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam (peace be upon him), with the words: "Dhalika min anba'il-ghaybi nuhihi ilayk."

He says: these, O Messenger of Allah, are unknown tidings, tidings of the unseen. "Wa ma kunta ladayhim idh ajma'u amrahum wa hum yamkurun." And He says: you were not, O Messenger, with Yusuf's brothers when they gathered, or came together, to plot against Yusuf, in order to throw him into the well. So He says: you could not have known this in any other way except through revelation, except

in the way that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, reveals it to you. There is no other way to know this except revelation. It is from Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, who knows what has been and what will be. But, He says, most of your people will not believe you in this.
وَمَا تَسْأَلُهُمْ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ أَجْرٍ ۚ إِنْ هُوَ إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ لِلْعَالَمِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “And you do not ask them for any reward for it; it is nothing but a reminder to the worlds.” (Yusuf 12:104)

segmenti.tekst: He says: you, O Messenger of Allah, do not ask for a reward, a payment, for this Qur'an. "In huwa illa dhikrun lil-'alamin" – truly, He says, it is only a reminder to the worlds. Truly, the Qur'an is only a reminder to the worlds. "Wa ma aktharun-nasi wa law harasta bi mu'minin. Wa ma tas'aluhum 'alayhi min ajrin, in huwa illa dhikrun lil-'alamin. Wa ka'ayyin min ayatin fis-samawati wal-ardi yamurruna 'alayha wa hum 'anha mu'ridun." He says: there are many signs,
many proofs, He says, proofs in the heavens and on the Earth, which those same mushrikun (idolaters), but also other people, pass by; they see them, but they do not reflect on them.

There are many proofs, dear brothers, that point to Allah's oneness, that He alone is the one Creator, that He is the One who deserves to be worshipped, but people do not grasp it; they will not reflect.

Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says in another ayah: "Inna fi khalqis-samawati wal-ardi wakhtilafil-layli wan-nahari la-ayatin li ulil-albab." He says: truly, in the creation of the heavens and the Earth and the alternation of night and day, He says, there is proof for people who have understanding, proof for people who have understanding, who use their minds. And Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, mentions in many ayat, He says: "wa lakinna aktharan-nasi la ya'qilun" – but, He says, most people do not use their reason; "la yatafakkarun" – He says, but most people do not reflect, will not reflect.

"Yamurruna 'alayha wa hum 'anha mu'ridun." Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, then says to the Prophet, after these ayat: "Qul hadhihi sabili ad'u ilallah" – say, O Messenger of Allah: this is my way, this is the way to which I invite,
عَلَىٰ بَصِيرَةٍ أَنَا وَمَنِ اتَّبَعَنِي
segmenti.prevod: “…with clear insight, I and those who follow me…” (Yusuf 12:108)

segmenti.tekst: with clear proofs. The way to which I invite, and that is the way of Islam, of iman, of faith and of worshipping Allah alone, subhanahu wa ta'ala. With clear proofs.

So what the Prophet Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, invited to, he invited to with clear proofs, with irrefutable proofs. And to this very day no one can refute that proof. Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Qul la'inijtama'atil-insu wal-jinnu 'ala an ya'tu bi mithli hadhal-Qur'ani la ya'tuna bi mithlihi wa law kana ba'duhum li ba'din zahira."
And He says: say, if jinn and mankind were to gather together to produce something like the Qur'an, He says, they could not do it. Even if they were, He says, helpers, helpers to one another.
After that, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, [unclear] His Messenger, He says:
حَتَّىٰ إِذَا اسْتَيْأَسَ الرُّسُلُ وَظَنُّوا أَنَّهُمْ قَدْ كُذِبُوا جَاءَهُمْ نَصْرُنَا فَنُجِّيَ مَنْ نَشَاءُ ۖ وَلَا يُرَدُّ بَأْسُنَا عَنِ الْقَوْمِ الْمُجْرِمِينَ
segmenti.prevod: “Until, when the messengers despaired and thought that they had been denied, Our help came to them, and whoever We willed was saved; and Our punishment cannot be turned back from the criminal people.” (Yusuf 12:110)

segmenti.tekst: And He says: when the messengers thought, O Muhammad, that help would not come to them, when they had lost hope that their people would believe in them, when they thought they had been denied – "ja'ahum nasruna" – He says, Our help came to them. So Our help will come to you too, O Muhammad; do not worry.

So for the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam… And we said that this surah was revealed to the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, at the most difficult time. So there was no… it was the peak, the peak of torment and persecution in Mecca. And after this, that is, after this surah, or not long after this surah, Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, permitted the Prophet to make the hijrah to Medina.
And then Islam grew strong. After that Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, says: "Truly, in the stories of these messengers there is a lesson and a teaching for those who have understanding."

Again: a lesson for those who have understanding. I have mentioned before that for us, that is, the Qur'an was sent so that we would take lessons from it, so that we would read it, take lessons from it, keep company with it.

And you will see, dear brothers, when a person immerses himself a little more deeply in the Qur'an, when he reads it and reflects on it, every time he learns something new, every time he draws some new fa'ida, some benefit from the Qur'an.

And every time, here, let us say, every time you read Surah Yusuf, every time you live through the story of Surah Yusuf anew, as if you were hearing it for the first time. As if you were hearing it for the first time.

And that is also [unclear] the lesson, that a person takes lessons from the Qur'an. And with this ayah we have completed a chapter, a beautiful surah, Surah Yusuf, with which we have spent time during this month of Ramadan.
But, dear brothers, just as Ya'qub and his children and Yusuf passed away, and this Qur'an – that is, just as our Prophet, to whom this Qur'an was revealed, passed away – so too shall we pass away.

So too shall we pass away; we only choose whether we will be remembered for good or for bad. And, dear brothers, there is nothing wrong with a person asking Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, that people remember him for good after, after his death.

"Waj'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin, waj'al li lisana sidqin fil-akhirin" – when Ibrahim, alayhis-salam, prayed to Allah: "My Lord," he said, "cause the generations that come after my death," he said, "to remember me for good."
And we too, dear brothers, will soon meet our Lord. Many of those who fasted this month of Ramadan will not live to see the next one.

Many. And in that there is a lesson and [unclear], that a person should know that this world is passing. And everything that passes, everything that passes – a person should not worry too much; rather, he should look at where he will end up, how he will end, in what way he will end, whether he will have a good ending or an ugly ending. That is why, dear brothers, we ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and to make us firm on this path.

Ask Him, the Exalted, that we may live to see many more Ramadans, like this, as I said, and in this company, this beautiful company, that we may spend much, much more time together, that we may enjoy these blessings Allah has given us, that is, the blessings of guidance, of iman, of Islam. How many there are who have passed away, who would give everything just to be here with us now.

Let us also not be, dear brothers, among those… it is [unclear] that we be among those about whom the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, says: "al-mustarih" – the one who, when he leaves this world, is, finds rest.

You know, our elders say: "He has found rest." And who has found rest? The one who prayed the five prayers, who gave zakat, who performed the Hajj has found rest. He has found rest; not everyone finds rest. And the Prophet says: "wal-mustarahu minh."

He says: do not be, he says, among those from whom people will find rest. So a person should strive to be among the good ones. When he is not at the mosque for one day, or two, the efendi should ask him: "Where have you been?", or another member of the congregation: "Has this man [unclear], why isn't he here, where is he, how is he?"

We must not, dear brothers, be among those who – as if, whether he came to the mosque or not – and if the man does not come, the congregation is glad: "Thank Allah, he's not here, [unclear]. He insults us, he causes us problems," and so on.

A person must not be one of those. Then there is some big, big, big problem there. Rather, we should be among the true, good, good believers: when we leave this world, let us be among those who found rest, and not among those from whom others found rest. And we ask Allah, subhanahu wa ta'ala, to forgive our sins and the sins of our parents, and to admit us into Jannah (Paradise). Amin, ya Rabbal-'alamin. As-salamu alaykum wa rahmatullahi ta'ala wa barakatuh.
